top_cited_works.title: Molecular dynamics simulation of rotational relaxation in nitrogen: Implications for rotational collision number models
top_cited_works.abstract: We study the rotational relaxation process in nitrogen using all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC). The intermolecular model used in the MD simulations is shown to (i) reproduce very well the shear viscosity of nitrogen over a wide range of temperatures, (ii) predict the near-equilibrium rotational collision number in good agreement with published trajectory calculations done on ab initio potential energy surfaces, and (iii) produce shock wave profiles in excellent accordance with the experimental measurements. We find that the rotational relaxation process is dependent not only on the near-equilibrium temperature (i.e., when systems relax to equilibrium after a small perturbation), but more importantly on both the magnitude and direction of the initial deviation from the equilibrium state. The comparison between MD and DSMC, based on the Borgnakke-Larsen model, for shock waves (both at low and high temperatures) and one-dimensional expansions shows that a judicious choice of a constant Zrot can produce DSMC results which are in relatively good agreement with MD. top_cited_works.title: Rapid Targeted Next-Generation Sequencing Platform for Molecular Screening and Clinical Genotyping in Subjects with Hemoglobinopathies
top_cited_works.abstract: Hemoglobinopathies are among the most common autosomal-recessive disorders worldwide. A comprehensive next-generation sequencing (NGS) test would greatly facilitate screening and diagnosis of these disorders. An NGS panel targeting the coding regions of hemoglobin genes and four modifier genes was designed. We validated the assay by using 2522 subjects affected with hemoglobinopathies and applied it to carrier testing in a cohort of 10,111 couples who were also screened through traditional methods. In the clinical genotyping analysis of 1182 β-thalassemia subjects, we identified a group of additional variants that can be used for accurate diagnosis. In the molecular screening analysis of the 10,111 couples, we detected 4180 individuals in total who carried 4840 mutant alleles, and identified 186 couples at risk of having affected offspring. 12.1% of the pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants identified by our NGS assay, which were undetectable by traditional methods. Compared with the traditional methods, our assay identified an additional at-risk 35 couples. recent_works.title: Modeling of Rarefied and Weakly Ionized Hypersonic Flows Using the Direct Simulation Monte Carlo Method
recent_works.abstract: During atmospheric entry, a plasma layer with ions and electrons forms around the vehicle surfaces, evident from the radio communication blackout. In this paper, the direct simulation Monte Carlo method is used to model the plasma formation in rarefied and weakly ionized hypersonic flow. The first objective is to implement and numerically verify existing high-temperature chemical kinetic models in the recently developed direct simulation Monte Carlo / particle-in-cell code, Comet. This code works on either the CPU or GPU devices, and uses a distributed unstructured mesh. It achieves large-scale parallel computing and is able to handle complex simulation geometry. The second objective is to numerically investigate the plasma formation of a canonical hypersonic vehicle geometry at representative Earth entry flight conditions, which used the two-dimensional hypersonic flow over a circular cylinder geometry at 81 km altitude. It can serve as a common test case for future chemical kinetic model comparisons between different computational codes. recent_works.title: Numerical Validation and Simulation of Velocity Slip and Temperature Jump in Hypersonic Non-Equilibrium Flow Using the Direct Simulation Monte Carlo Method
recent_works.abstract: Velocity slip and temperature jump on the wall surface are important features of hypersonic flow at low density. They affect aerodynamic force and heat transfer to the wall surface. Accurately simulating such flow with continuum computational fluid dynamics method requires the proper specification of boundary conditions on the wall surface. The correct quantification of velocity slip and temperature jump effects in numerical simulation can only be achieved by considering the kinetic nature of the gas, where the direct simulation Monte Carlo method is usually used. A recently developed direct simulation Monte Carlo code, Comet, is used to numerically study the velocity slip and temperature jump of hypersonic flow passing a flat plate surface. The first objective of this paper is to validate the Comet simulation results with existing experimental data. The second objective is to report the velocity slip and temperature jump of flat plate geometry at various Knudsen numbers and Mach numbers. It is anticipated that, the extensive simulation results presented in this paper can be used to develop new slip boundary condition model in computational fluid dynamics simulations.

recent_works.title: Comet-3D: GPU-Accelerated Three-Dimensional Direct Simulation Monte Carlo Code Using Unstructured Mesh
recent_works.abstract: We report the development of the three-dimensional version of the Comet code, a recently developed direct simulation Monte Carlo code for modeling rarefied gas flow and hypersonic flow. In a previous paper, we reported the two-dimensional version of the Comet code, including the distributed unstructured mesh, particle data structure, and numerical algorithms to perform major operations on the GPU accelerators. Comet takes a mesh-centric approach to achieve good computing performance on the GPU accelerators, where each simulation particle is associated with a mesh element or a simulation cell. However, extending Comet to three dimensions poses additional challenges, including three-dimensional unstructured mesh generation, distributed mesh partition, mesh adaptation, and results post-processing and visualization. In this paper, we first briefly discuss the direct simulation Monte Carlo method and the simulation work flow of Comet. Comet: Development of an Unstructured Mesh Direct Simulation Monte Carlo Code on GPUs
recent_works.abstract: In this paper, we report the development of Comet, a new direct simulation Monte Carlo code for modeling rarefied gas flow and hypersonic flow. This paper focuses on the data structures and the GPU computing framework of the two-dimensional code. Comet uses a distributed unstructured mesh, works fully on the GPU accelerators, and aims at large-scale simulations. It takes a mesh-centric approach, where each simulation particle is associated with a mesh element or a simulation cell. Data of all simulation particles belong to the same mesh element is grouped together, stored in continuous memory location, and is associated with a mesh element of the distributed mesh. The mesh and particle data structures used in this code attain good memory usage and data locality, allowing the code to achieve good computing performance on the GPU accelerators. We first discuss the mesh and particle data structures used in this code. Secondly, we outline the numerical algorithm framework in Comet, including particle data structure needed to implement particle collision models.
